import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.16

by L. A. Kurdachenko

A class of groups is called a *direct variety* if it is closed under taking subgroups,
factor-groups, and direct products (Yu. M. Gorchakov, *Groups with Finite Classes of Conjugate
Elements*, Moscow, Nauka, 1978 (Russian)). It is obvious that the class of $FC$-groups is a
direct variety. P. Hall (*J. London Math. Soc.*, **34**, no. 3 (1959), 289–304) showed that the
class of finite groups and the class of abelian groups taken together do not generate the class
of $FC$-groups as a direct variety, and it was shown in (L. A. Kurdachenko, *Ukrain. Math. J.*,
**39**, no. 3 (1987), 255–259) that the direct variety of $FC$-groups is also not generated by
the class of groups with finite derived subgroups. Is the direct variety of $FC$-groups generated
by the class of groups with finite derived subgroups together with the class of $FC$-groups
having quasicyclic derived subgroups?

Here an $FC$-group is a group in which every element has only finitely many conjugates, and a
quasicyclic group is a Prüfer group $\mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for some prime $p$. "Direct product"
means the restricted direct product (only finitely many non-identity coordinates) over an
arbitrary index set: unrestricted Cartesian products of infinitely many non-abelian finite
groups are not $FC$-groups, so with unrestricted products the class of $FC$-groups would not be
a direct variety.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped RestrictedProduct

namespace Kourovka.«10.16»

universe u

/-- A group $G$ is an $FC$-group if every element of $G$ has only finitely many conjugates. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (conjugatesOf g).Finite

/-- A group is *quasicyclic* if it is a Prüfer group $\mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for some prime $p$,
i.e. isomorphic to the group of all complex $p^n$-th roots of unity, $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$. -/
def IsQuasicyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* ↥(⨆ n : ℕ, rootsOfUnity (p ^ n) ℂ))

/-- A class of groups (in the universe `u`), given as a predicate on groups. -/
abbrev GroupClass : Type (u + 1) :=
  ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], Prop

/-- A class of groups is a *direct variety* if it is closed under taking isomorphic copies,
subgroups, factor-groups, and restricted direct products $\prod^{\text{res}}_{i \in I} G_i$
(all $x = (x_i)_{i \in I}$ with $x_i = 1$ for all but finitely many $i$) over arbitrary index
sets $I$. -/
structure IsDirectVariety (𝓒 : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop where
  of_mulEquiv : ∀ {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H], G ≃* H → 𝓒 G → 𝓒 H
  subgroup : ∀ {G : Type u} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G), 𝓒 G → 𝓒 H
  quotient : ∀ {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], 𝓒 G → 𝓒 (G ⧸ N)
  restrictedProduct : ∀ {ι : Type u} {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Group (G i)],
    (∀ i, 𝓒 (G i)) → 𝓒 (Πʳ i, [G i, (⊥ : Subgroup (G i))])

/-- The direct variety generated by a class of groups `𝓧`: the smallest direct variety
containing `𝓧`, i.e. the intersection of all direct varieties containing `𝓧`. -/
def directVarietyClosure (𝓧 : GroupClass.{u}) : GroupClass.{u} :=
  fun G _ => ∀ 𝓒 : GroupClass.{u},
    IsDirectVariety 𝓒 → (∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], 𝓧 H → 𝓒 H) → 𝓒 G

/--
Is the direct variety of $FC$-groups generated by the class of groups with finite derived
subgroups together with the class of $FC$-groups having quasicyclic derived subgroups?

That is, is the smallest class of groups closed under isomorphic copies, subgroups,
factor-groups and restricted direct products (over arbitrary index sets) that contains every
group $G$ with $G'$ finite and every $FC$-group $G$ with $G' \cong \mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for
some prime $p$ exactly the class of $FC$-groups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      directVarietyClosure
        (fun (H : Type) [Group H] =>
          Finite (commutator H) ∨ (IsFCGroup H ∧ IsQuasicyclic (commutator H))) G ↔
      IsFCGroup G := by
  sorry

/-- Every finite group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFCGroup_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsFCGroup G :=
  fun _ => Set.toFinite _

/-- Every abelian group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFCGroup_of_isMulCommutative (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsMulCommutative G] :
    IsFCGroup G :=
  fun g => (Set.finite_singleton g).subset fun _ hb => by simpa [eq_comm] using isConj_iff_eq.mp hb

/-- Every group with finite derived subgroup is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_finite_commutator (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite (commutator G)] :
    IsFCGroup G := fun g => by
  refine ((commutator G : Set G).toFinite.image (g * ·)).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  refine ⟨⁅g⁻¹, c⁆,
    Subgroup.commutator_mem_commutator (Subgroup.mem_top _) (Subgroup.mem_top _), ?_⟩
  simp [commutatorElement_def, mul_assoc]

/-- The group of all complex $2^n$-th roots of unity is quasicyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isQuasicyclic_rootsOfUnity_two : IsQuasicyclic ↥(⨆ n : ℕ, rootsOfUnity (2 ^ n) ℂ) :=
  ⟨2, Nat.prime_two, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- The direct variety generated by `𝓧` contains `𝓧`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_directVarietyClosure {𝓧 : GroupClass.{u}} {G : Type u} [Group G] (hG : 𝓧 G) :
    directVarietyClosure 𝓧 G :=
  fun _ _ h𝓧 => h𝓧 G hG

/-- The direct variety generated by `𝓧` is a direct variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isDirectVariety_directVarietyClosure (𝓧 : GroupClass.{u}) :
    IsDirectVariety (directVarietyClosure 𝓧) where
  of_mulEquiv e hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.of_mulEquiv e (hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧)
  subgroup H hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.subgroup H (hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧)
  quotient N _ hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.quotient N (hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧)
  restrictedProduct hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.restrictedProduct fun i => hG i 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧

/-- An isomorphic copy of an $FC$-group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] (e : G ≃* H) (hG : IsFCGroup G) :
    IsFCGroup H := fun h => by
  refine ((hG (e.symm h)).image e).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  exact ⟨e.symm b, isConj_iff.mpr ⟨e.symm c, by simpa using congrArg e.symm hc⟩, by simp⟩

/-- A subgroup of an $FC$-group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.subgroup {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsFCGroup G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    IsFCGroup H := fun h => by
  refine ((hG h).preimage Subtype.val_injective.injOn).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  exact isConj_iff.mpr ⟨c, by simpa using congrArg Subtype.val hc⟩

/-- A factor-group of an $FC$-group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.quotient {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsFCGroup G) (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] :
    IsFCGroup (G ⧸ N) := fun g => by
  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective g
  refine ((hG g).image (QuotientGroup.mk (s := N))).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective c
  exact ⟨c * g * c⁻¹, isConj_iff.mpr ⟨c, rfl⟩, by simpa using hc⟩

/-- A restricted direct product of $FC$-groups is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.restrictedProduct {ι : Type*} {G : ι → Type*} [∀ i, Group (G i)]
    (hG : ∀ i, IsFCGroup (G i)) : IsFCGroup (Πʳ i, [G i, (⊥ : Subgroup (G i))]) := fun x => by
  have hS : {i | x i ≠ 1}.Finite := by simpa using x.2
  have hsub : ∀ y ∈ conjugatesOf x, ∀ i, x i = 1 → y i = 1 := by
    intro y hy i hi
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hy
    show c i * x i * (c i)⁻¹ = 1
    simp [hi]
  refine Set.Finite.of_finite_image (f := fun y (i : hS.toFinset) => y i) ?_ ?_
  · refine (Set.Finite.pi' (t := fun (i : hS.toFinset) => conjugatesOf (x i))
      (fun i => hG _ _)).subset ?_
    rintro _ ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ i
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hy
    exact isConj_iff.mpr ⟨c i, rfl⟩
  · intro y hy z hz h
    ext i
    by_cases hi : x i = 1
    · rw [hsub y hy i hi, hsub z hz i hi]
    · exact congrFun h ⟨i, hS.mem_toFinset.mpr hi⟩

/-- "It is obvious that the class of $FC$-groups is a direct variety." -/
@[category textbook, AMS 20]
theorem isDirectVariety_isFCGroup :
    IsDirectVariety (fun (G : Type u) [Group G] => IsFCGroup G) where
  of_mulEquiv e hG := hG.of_mulEquiv e
  subgroup H hG := hG.subgroup H
  quotient N _ hG := hG.quotient N
  restrictedProduct hG := IsFCGroup.restrictedProduct hG

end Kourovka.«10.16»

by L. A. Kurdachenko

The direct product of an arbitrary family of groups is the *restricted* direct product
(the subgroup of the Cartesian product consisting of the families with finite support);
this is the only reading under which the class of $FC$-groups is a direct variety, since
the unrestricted Cartesian product of infinitely many non-abelian finite groups is not an
$FC$-group. A quasicyclic group is a Prüfer group $C_{p^\infty}$ for some prime $p$.

open scoped RestrictedProduct

namespace Kourovka.«10.16»

/-- A class of groups: a predicate on groups (in universe `Type`). -/
abbrev GroupClass := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop

/-- A group $G$ is an *$FC$-group* if every element of $G$ has only finitely many conjugates. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, {h : G | IsConj g h}.Finite

/-- The quasicyclic (Prüfer) $p$-group $C_{p^\infty}$, realised as the group of all complex
$p^n$-th roots of unity, $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$. -/
def pruferGroup (p : ℕ) : Subgroup ℂˣ :=
  ⨆ n : ℕ, rootsOfUnity (p ^ n) ℂ

/-- A group is *quasicyclic* if it is isomorphic to the Prüfer group $C_{p^\infty}$ for some
prime $p$. -/
def IsQuasicyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* pruferGroup p)

/-- A class of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ is a *direct variety* if it is closed under isomorphic
images, taking subgroups, taking factor-groups, and taking (restricted) direct products of
arbitrary families of its members. The restricted direct product of the family `G i` is the
subgroup `Πʳ i, [G i, ⊥]` of `Π i, G i` consisting of the families with finite support. -/
structure IsDirectVariety (𝓧 : GroupClass) : Prop where
  of_mulEquiv : ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], G ≃* H → 𝓧 G → 𝓧 H
  subgroup : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (H : Subgroup G), 𝓧 G → 𝓧 H
  quotient : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], 𝓧 G → 𝓧 (G ⧸ N)
  restrictedProduct : ∀ (ι : Type) (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, Group (G i)],
    (∀ i, 𝓧 (G i)) → 𝓧 (Πʳ i, [G i, (⊥ : Subgroup (G i))])

/-- The direct variety generated by a class of groups $\mathfrak{X}$: the smallest direct
variety containing $\mathfrak{X}$, i.e. the intersection of all direct varieties containing
$\mathfrak{X}$. -/
def directVarietyGenerated (𝓧 : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  fun G _ => ∀ 𝓨 : GroupClass, IsDirectVariety 𝓨 →
    (∀ (H : Type) [Group H], 𝓧 H → 𝓨 H) → 𝓨 G

/-- The class of groups with finite derived subgroup, taken together with the class of
$FC$-groups with quasicyclic derived subgroup. -/
def generatingClass : GroupClass :=
  fun G _ => Finite (commutator G) ∨ (IsFCGroup G ∧ IsQuasicyclic (commutator G))

/--
Is the direct variety of $FC$-groups generated by the class of groups with finite derived
subgroups together with the class of $FC$-groups having quasicyclic derived subgroups?

That is, does the smallest class of groups that contains every group with finite derived
subgroup and every $FC$-group with quasicyclic derived subgroup, and that is closed under
taking subgroups, factor-groups and (restricted) direct products of arbitrary families,
coincide with the class of all $FC$-groups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (IsFCGroup G ↔ directVarietyGenerated generatingClass G) := by
  sorry

/-- "It is obvious that the class of $FC$-groups is a direct variety." -/
@[category textbook, AMS 20]
theorem isDirectVariety_isFCGroup : IsDirectVariety fun G _ => IsFCGroup G := by
  sorry

@[category API]
theorem mem_pruferGroup {p : ℕ} {z : ℂˣ} :
    z ∈ pruferGroup p ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, z ^ p ^ n = 1 := by
  rw [pruferGroup, Subgroup.mem_iSup_of_directed]
  · simp [mem_rootsOfUnity]
  · exact Monotone.directed_le fun m n hmn => rootsOfUnity_le_of_dvd (pow_dvd_pow p hmn)

@[category API]
theorem isFCGroup_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsFCGroup G :=
  fun _ => Set.toFinite _

@[category API]
theorem isFCGroup_of_isMulCommutative (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsMulCommutative G] :
    IsFCGroup G := by
  intro g
  refine (Set.finite_singleton g).subset fun h hh => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hh
  simp [mul_comm]

@[category API]
theorem isDirectVariety_directVarietyGenerated (𝓧 : GroupClass) :
    IsDirectVariety (directVarietyGenerated 𝓧) where
  of_mulEquiv G H _ _ e hG 𝓨 h𝓨 h𝓧 := h𝓨.of_mulEquiv G H e (hG 𝓨 h𝓨 h𝓧)
  subgroup G _ H hG 𝓨 h𝓨 h𝓧 := h𝓨.subgroup G H (hG 𝓨 h𝓨 h𝓧)
  quotient G _ N _ hG 𝓨 h𝓨 h𝓧 := h𝓨.quotient G N (hG 𝓨 h𝓨 h𝓧)
  restrictedProduct ι G _ hG 𝓨 h𝓨 h𝓧 :=
    h𝓨.restrictedProduct ι G fun i => hG i 𝓨 h𝓨 h𝓧

@[category API]
theorem le_directVarietyGenerated (𝓧 : GroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] (hG : 𝓧 G) :
    directVarietyGenerated 𝓧 G :=
  fun _ _ h => h G hG

@[category API]
theorem directVarietyGenerated_le (𝓧 𝓨 : GroupClass) (h𝓨 : IsDirectVariety 𝓨)
    (h : ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], 𝓧 H → 𝓨 H) (G : Type) [Group G]
    (hG : directVarietyGenerated 𝓧 G) : 𝓨 G :=
  hG 𝓨 h𝓨 h

end Kourovka.«10.16»

# Conjecture 10.16

by L. A. Kurdachenko

A class of groups is called a *direct variety* if it is closed under taking subgroups,
factor-groups, and direct products (Yu. M. Gorchakov, *Groups with Finite Classes of
Conjugate Elements*, Moscow, Nauka, 1978 (Russian)). It is obvious that the class of
$FC$-groups is a direct variety. P. Hall (*J. London Math. Soc.* **34**, no. 3 (1959),
289–304) showed that the class of finite groups and the class of abelian groups taken
together do not generate the class of $FC$-groups as a direct variety, and it was shown in
(L. A. Kurdachenko, *Ukrain. Math. J.* **39**, no. 3 (1987), 255–259) that the direct
variety of $FC$-groups is also not generated by the class of groups with finite derived
subgroups. Is the direct variety of $FC$-groups generated by the class of groups with finite
derived subgroups together with the class of $FC$-groups having quasicyclic derived
subgroups?

Conventions used below:

* An $FC$-group is a group in which every element has only finitely many conjugates.
* "Direct product" means the *restricted* direct product over an arbitrary index set, i.e. the
  subgroup of the Cartesian product consisting of the elements with all but finitely many
  coordinates trivial. (The unrestricted Cartesian product of infinitely many non-abelian
  finite groups is not an $FC$-group, so with Cartesian products the class of $FC$-groups
  would not be a direct variety.)

  realised here as the group of all complex $p^n$-th roots of unity ($n \in \mathbb{N}$).

  it, i.e. the intersection of all direct varieties containing it.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

subgroups, factor-groups and (restricted) direct products over arbitrary index sets. As is
standard for classes of groups, $\mathfrak{X}$ is also required to be closed under isomorphism.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.16

by L. A. Kurdachenko

A direct variety is a class of groups closed under subgroups, quotient groups,
and restricted direct products over arbitrary index sets. Is the direct variety
of $FC$-groups generated by the groups with finite derived subgroup together
with the $FC$-groups whose derived subgroup is quasicyclic?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.16»

universe u

/-- A group is an $FC$-group if every conjugacy class is finite. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, {h : G | ∃ x : G, h = x * g * x⁻¹}.Finite

/-- A group is quasicyclic if it is a Prüfer $p$-group for some prime $p$. -/
def IsQuasicyclic (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ ∃ x : ℕ → G,
    (∀ n : ℕ, orderOf (x n) = p ^ (n + 1)) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, x (n + 1) ^ p = x n) ∧
    ∀ g : G, ∃ n : ℕ, g ∈ Subgroup.zpowers (x n)

/-- The restricted direct product of a family of groups: the subgroup of the
Cartesian product consisting of the functions with finite multiplicative support. -/
def restrictedDirectProduct {ι : Type u} (G : ι → Type u) [∀ i, Group (G i)] :
    Subgroup (∀ i, G i) where
  carrier := {f : ∀ i, G i | Set.Finite {i | f i ≠ 1}}
  one_mem' := by simp
  mul_mem' := by
    intro f g hf hg
    apply (hf.union hg).subset
    intro i hi
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_union, Pi.mul_apply] at hi ⊢
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    exact hi (by rw [h.1, h.2, one_mul])
  inv_mem' := by
    intro f hf
    change Set.Finite {i | (f i)⁻¹ ≠ 1}
    change Set.Finite {i | f i ≠ 1} at hf
    simpa only [inv_ne_one] using hf

/-- A property of groups in one universe. The group structure is an explicit
argument so that properties can themselves be quantified over. -/
def GroupProperty := ∀ (G : Type u), Group G → Prop

/-- A group property holds for a group with its given group structure. -/
def GroupProperty.Holds (C : GroupProperty.{u}) (G : Type u) [g : Group G] : Prop :=
  C G g

/-- A direct variety is an isomorphism-invariant class of groups closed under
subgroups, quotient groups, and arbitrary-index restricted direct products. -/
def IsDirectVariety (C : GroupProperty.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∀ (G H : Type u) [Group G] [Group H], C.Holds G → (G ≃* H) → C.Holds H) ∧
  (∀ (G : Type u) [Group G] (H : Subgroup G), C.Holds G → C.Holds H) ∧
  (∀ (G : Type u) [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal],
    C.Holds G → C.Holds (G ⧸ N)) ∧
  ∀ (ι : Type u) (G : ι → Type u) [∀ i, Group (G i)],
    (∀ i, C.Holds (G i)) → C.Holds (restrictedDirectProduct G)

/-- The direct variety generated by the groups with finite derived subgroup
and the $FC$-groups with quasicyclic derived subgroup. -/
def InGeneratedDirectVariety (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ C : GroupProperty.{u}, IsDirectVariety C →
    (∀ (H : Type u) [Group H],
      (Finite (commutator H) ∨
        (IsFCGroup H ∧ IsQuasicyclic (commutator H))) → C.Holds H) →
    C.Holds G

/--
Is the direct variety of $FC$-groups generated by the class of groups with
finite derived subgroups together with the class of $FC$-groups having
quasicyclic derived subgroups (that is, Prüfer $p$-groups for some prime $p$)?
Here direct products are restricted direct products over arbitrary index sets.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], IsFCGroup G → InGeneratedDirectVariety G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.16»
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “direct products” as finite-support (restricted) direct products over arbitrary index types, as required by the decomposition; the product is represented as a subgroup of the dependent Cartesian product.

Made direct varieties explicitly invariant under multiplicative group isomorphism. This captures the usual meaning of a class of groups and prevents the generated class from depending on concrete Lean carrier types.
Defined membership in the generated direct variety impredicatively: a group belongs exactly when it belongs to every direct variety containing both generating classes.
Used the intrinsic characterization of a quasicyclic group as a Prüfer p-group generated by a compatible chain x_n of orders p^(n+1), with x_(n+1)^p = x_n.

Stated the requested equality as inclusion of every FC-group in the generated direct variety. This is equivalent because the FC-groups form a direct variety containing both generating classes, as specified in the decomposition notes.
All group classes and closure operations are universe-polymorphic but operate within one fixed Lean universe at a time.

new_definitions.name: IsFCGroup
new_definitions.why_needed: Mathlib has conjugacy APIs but no predicate expressing that every conjugacy class of a group is finite.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib.Dynamics.FixedPoints.Prufer discusses Prüfer subgroups but does not define a reusable Prüfer group; IsPGroup alone is much weaker.
new_definitions.name: IsQuasicyclic
new_definitions.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib provides quasicyclic/Prüfer p-groups as a group predicate or canonical group type.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: DFinsupp and DirectSum are zero/additive-oriented, and Function.mulSupport only handles a nondependent codomain; neither directly supplies the required dependent multiplicative group.
new_definitions.name: restrictedDirectProduct
new_definitions.why_needed: The conjecture requires finite-support multiplicative products of arbitrary families of potentially nonabelian groups.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Bundled GrpCat classes were considered, but no existing direct-variety closure abstraction was found.
new_definitions.name: GroupProperty
new_definitions.why_needed: The smallest class of groups must quantify over properties while retaining each carrier's group structure.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Direct application of GroupProperty with inferInstance, which is less readable throughout the closure conditions.
new_definitions.name: GroupProperty.Holds
new_definitions.why_needed: Provides typeclass-friendly application of an explicitly structured GroupProperty.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Generic closure operators and category-theoretic GrpCat constructions; none expresses this exact nonstandard notion of direct variety.
new_definitions.name: IsDirectVariety
new_definitions.why_needed: No existing predicate packages isomorphism invariance and closure under subgroups, normal quotients, and restricted direct products.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: An inductively generated class; the intersection-of-all-closed-classes formulation states the smallest direct variety more directly.
new_definitions.name: InGeneratedDirectVariety
new_definitions.why_needed: No existing generated-closure construction captures this exact combination of group operations and the two seed classes.
